evidence.locator: Pages 1–2 and 11: Bolama first capital; Bissau capital transfer in 1941
evidence.note: The archival account dates separation from Cape Verde to 18 March 1879 and identifies Bolama as the first capital until the 1941 transfer. Only the existing colony framework is covered.

qualifications: Not the modern Guinea-Bissau capital projected backwards. Capital transition year 1941 is retained at year precision; 1880 remains a partial editorial boundary under scanner policy.

claims.value: Portuguese colonial military campaigns led by João Teixeira Pinto began in March 1913 and continued into July 1915.

scope.description: Explicit historical institution, office, affiliation or event of the named entity; not an inference about polygon sovereignty or statistical territory.

evidence.locator: Page 2: campaigns from March 1913 to July 1915
evidence.note: The archival history gives the campaign interval; the event record stores its actual starting month and explicitly preserves the subsequent duration.

qualifications: Selected 1914 snapshot receives dated 1913 context under existing rules; the start is not relabelled as 1914.
Military campaigns against local communities do not establish that the whole mapped colony had uniform effective sovereignty.
